text: Audit trail. Every entry has an audit trail. Nothing is edited silently.
Liability. The contract states where our liability begins and ends.
Confidentiality. Every analyst signs a confidentiality agreement on day one.
Data integrity. Data integrity is checked before every payroll run.
Scalable. The process is scalable. Forty employees or four hundred, it is the same process.
Regulatory. That is a regulatory deadline. We cannot move it.
Due diligence. Their due diligence took three weeks. We passed.
Breach. In a breach, we must notify you within 24 hours.
Head office sent a list. I’ll go through it quickly, if that’s all right.
Please do. If I can ’t answer something today, I’ll say so rather than guess.
Who can see our payroll data?
Three analysts and one partner. Everyone signs a confidentiality agreement, and every change leaves an audit trail.
And if there is a breach?
We must notify you within 24 hours. That is not our policy, it is regulatory.
Our auditors will want their own access.
We can give them read-only access. And you should keep a copy of the register on your side as well — not obligatory, just sensible.
Last one. We grow to two hundred people next year.

Fabia, this is the list from head office, so let me be precise about what is negotiable and what is not. Two things are non-negotiable. There must be a full audit trail on every change, and in the event of a breach we must be notified within twenty-four hours, in writing. Those two are not preferences, they are conditions of the group policy. Then there is one thing we recommend rather than require: there should be a quarterly call between your team and ours, so nobody discovers a problem in an email. And a warning on timing. Legal still has to review the contract, and that may take another two weeks. So please do not plan around signing this month.

So, they asked me who has access to the data, and I said, well, only a few people, usually. Then they asked what happens if there is a leak, and I said we would try to let them know as quickly as we could. And when they asked about their auditors, I said we could probably arrange something. I thought I was being honest. Looking back, every answer I gave sounded like a maybe. They asked for the same answers in writing, and after that they simply stopped replying. I lost that account on the words, not on the price.
